conviction_note: The findings roughly cancel. Against that, there is real support for another beat-and-raise: Q3 rail traffic ran above the H1 run-rate the guide assumed, and two Q3 service/loco orders were public. abs_move 6.0 (option event move 5.8, own median 4.6, last print +10.0) and p_up 52 give +0.24, close to the +0.3 findings sum. The two measurements agree that there is no edge.

findings.finding: The bar already sits above the company's own raised guide. H1 adj EPS was $5.47 ($2.71 + $2.76), so the $10.75 midpoint implies H2 of $5.28 (~$2.64 a quarter) and even the $10.90 top implies $5.43. Consensus is Q3 $2.72-2.74 and FY $10.87. The CFO guided Q3 adj margin expansion to only ~0.5pt (the H1 rate), with revenue growth slowing as Inspection Technologies laps. Q3 revenue consensus of $3.197bn (+10.8%) sits at the top of the range: the H2 midpoint implies ~+8% y/y. So an in-line quarter with a guide held, or raised by less than ~$0.15, reads as a miss against what is priced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 prints beat EPS and raised the FY guide. Q1 (beat $0.19, raise) bought +1.5%; Q2 (beat $0.13, revenue beat, +$0.30 midpoint raise) bought +10.0%. Oct-2025 Q3 beat-and-raise sold -2.3%. Feb-2025 guide disappointment was -9.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is partly priced. The skew is flat and the stock has drifted ~6% off August highs, which may already reflect some fatigue. But if the market saw the gap between the guide and the bar as risk, puts would be bid over calls and IV rank would not sit near its lows (tradestie says IV rank ~1). That indicates the street expects a routine third beat-and-raise.
findings.independence: The guide figures come from the company release (https://www.wabteccorp.com/newsroom/press-releases/wabtec-reports-strong-second-quarter-2026-results). The H1 EPS comes from the Q1 release (https://www.wabteccorp.com/newsroom/press-releases/wabtec-reports-first-quarter-2026-results). Consensus comes from two estimate sources. Cadence is from the call transcript.

findings.finding: U.S. rail traffic in Q3 and early Q4 ran above the run-rate under the July guide raise. Management said the revenue raise assumed the Q2 flow run-rate holds, with carloads up ~4% in Q2 and ~3% in H1. AAR weekly U.S. traffic was +13.8% (wk to Sep 5), -3.7% (Sep 12), +4.9% (Sep 19), +4.8% (Sep 26) and +7.2% (Oct 10, intermodal +10.4%, carloads +3.4%). YTD through week 40 combined traffic is +3.6%. This supports the aftermarket/flow business that drove the last raise, so a further FY revenue raise is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue raise, which management attributed to flow, coincided with the +10.0% reaction. No other print isolates this line.
findings.why_not_priced: AAR data is public weekly, so this is a broad series and largely in the estimates. FY revenue consensus ($12.55bn) already sits near the top of the guide. It would only be unpriced if the street has not lifted aftermarket assumptions. There is no sign of that in a flat 60-day estimate trend and a net-negative 30-day revision count (7 down / 6 up per tradestie).
findings.independence: This is a proxy: industry traffic, not Wabtec's own number. Corroborated by https://www.ajot.com/news/aar-reports-rail-traffic-for-the-week-ending-september-26-2026 and Progressive Railroading's week-40 report. The guide-assumption link comes from the call transcript shared with finding 1.

findings.finding: Two Q3 international orders were announced in the last ten days of the quarter. One is a >$700m long-term services agreement with La Compagnie du TransGuinéen for the Simandou Evolution fleet (2026-09-21), Wabtec's largest African services contract, taking Simandou business above $1.2bn. The other is a ~$254m (R$1.3bn) MRS Logística locomotives/parts/maintenance deal in Brazil (2026-09-23). Together these are ~$0.95bn of Q3 intake. They support the backlog headline (it was $30.93bn at Q2) and the services return to growth that management promised for H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog has printed at records (multi-year $30.8bn Q1, $30.93bn Q2). The Q2 record came with +10%, the Q1 record with +1.5%. Backlog alone has not been a reliable driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Both orders were press-released, so they are priced as facts. What is not visible is whether total Q3 orders hold the multi-year backlog flat-to-up after ~$3.2bn of quarterly revenue burn. Management flagged 'a couple of large' H2 deals; these two may be them, or there may be more. The stock fell rather than rose through late September, so the market did not treat them as a surprise.
findings.independence: MRS deal: https://www.railway.supply/mrs-logistica-follows-2024-wabtec-order-with-us254m-fleet-deal/ (2026-09-23). Simandou is also in https://www.miningweekly.com/article/wabtec-signs-700m-simandou-locomotive-services-agreement-2026-09-22.

findings.finding: Greenbrier's fiscal Q4 (Jun-Aug 2026) railcar orders rose to 3,400 cars (~$600m) from 2,200 cars ($340m) the prior quarter. This is an early sign that the North American railcar trough Wabtec guided (~25,000 builds in 2026, -21%; railcars ~60% of Components; decline expected 'a couple more quarters') may be bottoming. That matters for any 2027 commentary on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Components have been a drag (-0.7% in Q2), offset elsewhere. No reaction has been isolated to railcar commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Public peer data, so mostly priced. It bears on Wabtec's 2027 tone, which could only matter if management chooses to discuss it on the call. Part of the order count is Saudi SAR (780 cars), not North American demand.
findings.independence: This is a proxy (peer orders). Wabtec's own railcar view is from https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WAB/Q22026 (shared with finding 1).

findings.finding: Refinancing ahead: the 10-Q shows $1.656bn current debt at 2026-06-30. That includes the $750m 3.45% senior notes due 2026-11-15 and a term loan maturing 2026-11-27. No 2026 refinancing issuance was found. Rolling 2016-vintage 3.45% paper at ~5% (the 2035 notes priced at 5.5% in May 2025) costs roughly $10-12m a year of interest, about $0.05 of EPS, mostly a 2027 item. Leverage is 2.2x, inside the 2-2.5x target, after Dellner and $457m of H1 buybacks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The May-2025 note issuance funded the Inspection Technologies acquisition with no visible reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The maturities are scheduled and visible in every credit model. I asked what the money buys: it is a rollover of existing debt, not distress or a new use. Signed zero.
findings.independence: Notes terms: https://www.davispolk.com/experience/westinghouse-air-brake-technologies-corporation-750-million-senior-notes-offering. This finding shares the 10-Q with no other finding.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no pattern. Routine post-print 10b5-1 sales recur (Feb 2026 cluster at ~$262-264, before the Q1 +1.5% print).
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and pre-planned. It carries no information and is filed for completeness.

baseline_tension: The evidence is balanced and agrees with the balanced skew (-0.61) and the mild negative run-up. Nothing cuts against the option market, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 'two readings of one document are one finding': the draft's EPS-bar finding (-0.6) and its Q3-cadence/revenue-bar finding (-0.4) rested on the same guide-versus-consensus arithmetic from one transcript. Merged into one guidance finding at -0.6.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the November note/term-loan rollover was moved from -0.1 to 0.0 after the answer: it refinances existing debt, leverage is 2.2x, and nothing is distressed.
Lesson 5 (proxy, smaller): AAR traffic trimmed from +0.6 to +0.5 and Greenbrier orders from +0.2 to +0.1, as industry/peer proxies not confirmed by Wabtec.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): Q3 orders trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3, because the backlog records have bought anywhere from +1.5% to +10%.
Lesson 6: the bar is verified by two agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, so no cap was applied. The insider-sale item was added at 0.0 so the panel sees it.
